title: Ship hardened production systemd unit presets
description: A systemd/ directory with production-hardened unit presets alongside the simple doc examples: DynamicUser=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, NoNewPrivileges=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX:AF_INET:AF_INET6, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, empty CapabilityBoundingSet, RestrictNamespaces=yes, LockPersonality=yes, ProtectKernelTuning/Modules/Hostname=yes, RestrictRealtime=yes, and Restart=on-failure tuned to the WatchdogSec budget documented in operations.md. Verify none of the sandboxing breaks the gateway's actual syscall surface (TLS, timers, sockets).
acceptance_criteria: Gateway serves under the preset with all directives active; systemd-analyze security exposure recorded; operations.md points at the shipped units.

title: systemd-native operation
description: Systemd integration for the gateway daemon: socket activation adopts the manager's ListenStream= socket, the shared password loads from $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY by credential name, and Type=notify units get READY/STATUS/STOPPING plus WatchdogSec heartbeats. Together these enable unit files that keep secrets out of argv and the environment, restart the gateway without refusing connections, and supervise it properly. Follow-ups when taken up (unix-socket ListenStream=, hardened unit presets, Type=notify-reload, fdstore) belong here.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway runs from .socket/.service units with credentials and notify, verified end-to-end; docs in operations.md 'systemd service integration'.

title: Public release: MIT license and GitHub publication
description: Publish opencode-bus-proxy as a public repository: MIT LICENSE file matching the declared workspace license, full history pushed to github.com/rektide/opencode-bus-proxy with main at tip, repository description and topics (rust, opencode, systemd, sse, server-sent-events, event-streaming, proxy, tokio, hyper, gateway). Pre-publication audit confirmed tracked .beads files are tooling boilerplate only; interaction logs and the dolt store are gitignored.
acceptance_criteria: Public repo serves main at the tip with license detected, description and topics set, no private data in history.
notes: Tip at publication: 2afd1ea7 'docs: document systemd integration and add the MIT license'.

title: Operations, verification, and architecture documentation
description: The maintained doc set: operations.md (topology, credentials, systemd integration, limits, failure behavior, tracing, verification interpretation), additive-verification.md and verification.md (current and earlier measurements including review corrections and performance evidence), design/event-multiplexer/* (architecture, additive-events contract, source contract, rust interfaces), crate READMEs, and the root README linking the canonical bus-smart architecture and handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Docs match shipped behavior; verification claims trace to recorded evidence; no stale references to removed routes (private source route, event-source.* envelopes).
notes: Representative commits: the docs: series throughout history ('docs: record router verification...', 'docs: record gateway verification review corrections and performance evidence', 'docs: explain gateway operation compatibility and limits', 'docs: link gateway references to the canonical bus-smart architecture').

title: Authenticated /_bus health, subscriptions, and metrics endpoints
description: Protected diagnostics: /_bus/health (source readiness, 503 while disconnected), /_bus/subscriptions (live legacy/pending/active subscriptions, followed Sessions, queue pressure; process-local identity only), /_bus/metrics (Prometheus counters and gauges for source traffic and routing admissions with bounded names, never Session-ID labels). All authenticated under the same native domain as the feeds.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoints answer only with valid native credentials; metrics names bounded; subscriptions snapshot reflects live state and invalidates across epochs.
notes: Implemented within the gateway transport work; contract documented in README.md 'Inspect' and operations.md 'Tracing and diagnostics'.

title: Daemon CLI, supervision, and graceful shutdown
description: The opencode-bus-proxy binary: clap CLI with env fallbacks for every operational knob (upstream/listen/username/password sources/CORS/limits/timeouts), tracing init with JSON mode, process supervision of router and gateway tasks, SIGINT/SIGTERM handling with a bounded shutdown grace before aborting stragglers, and join-shutdown for all stopped arms. Config validation errors are explicit and actionable at startup.
acceptance_criteria: Signals cancel source, routing actor, connections, and tunnels within the grace; startup misconfigurations name the offending source; API execution never inherits a short generic deadline.
notes: Representative commits: 'feat(cli): configure and supervise the Rust event gateway', 'fix(cli): expose connection bounds without timing out API execution'. Docs: README.md 'Run', operations.md 'Limits and failure behavior'.

title: Real-client compatibility suite against the compiled gateway
description: test/compatibility/clients.ts (Bun) checks the native and Rust copies of event-scope-v1.json are identical, then exercises the real bus-smart Bus, ordinary HTTP stream, and unchanged client/controller code against the compiled proxy: an isolated in-memory origin, one source connection serving multiple clients, native and updated decoders handling scoped events through the same routes. BUS_PROXY_BINARY overrides the binary under test; no managed services or model calls.
acceptance_criteria: Suite passes against the release binary; shared fixture hash equality enforced; legacy and bus-smart client flows verified through the same routes.
notes: Representative commits: 'test: verify real bus-smart and legacy clients through Rust gateway', 'Verify gateway loopback routing, source failures, auth and streaming trailers', 'test: verify shared raw event fixtures and browser-visible capabilities', 'Verify shared raw-wire scope cases and decoded SSE preservation', 'test: require ordinary scoped streams and shared delivery fixtures'. Docs: doc/event-multiplexer/additive-verification.md.

title: Redacted lifecycle tracing and classified source failures
description: Structured tracing with async-safe instrumentation: bounded redacted request and source lifecycle spans; source disconnects report fixed reason categories only - decoder/HTTP errors containing peer values, URLs, or event content must not enter logs; request/control debug tracing carries no bodies, credentials, or query strings; no per-recipient span in the token hot path. --log-json emits structured JSON; RUST_LOG filters both modes.
acceptance_criteria: Collected tracing exposes no password, credential, query string, or peer-supplied error text; failure categories are a closed set.
notes: Representative commits: 'Add redacted request and source lifecycle spans with async-safe instrumentation', 'fix(observability): classify source failures without logging peer data'. Docs: operations.md 'Tracing and diagnostics'.

title: Native-compatible auth and pairing sessions across the gateway
description: One shared OpenCode authorization domain: local feed and diagnostic routes accept native Basic/query credentials and password-signed pairing sessions (HMAC opencode-session-v1, port-scoped cookie names, Origin/Host checks) reimplemented byte-compatibly in Rust; forwarded requests retain caller credentials untouched; only the proxy's own source connection uses the configured service credential. Wrong-origin cookie use and missing credentials fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: A pairing token issued by native TypeScript auth succeeds on local diagnostics; wrong-origin cookies and missing credentials fail; credentials never appear in logs.
notes: Representative commits: 'test: validate native event schemas and pairing cookies across gateway', plus auth in 'Implement gateway source ownership...'. Docs: operations.md 'Credentials and browser compatibility', design/event-multiplexer/rust-interfaces.md.

title: Additive scoped events on the ordinary OpenCode stream
description: The contract pivot: ordinary events gain authoritative 'scope' on the ordinary GET /api/event uplink (OpenCode-Event-Scope: 1 capability header), replacing the earlier private source route and event-source.* envelopes. The gateway consumes negotiated scoped events, never guessing Session identity from payload fields; raw whole-event JSON is preserved downstream; legacy clients keep broadcast semantics. Specified, implemented, migrated, and conformance-recorded across bus-smart and this repo.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed-wire coverage targets additive event metadata; ordinary scoped streams and shared delivery fixtures required by tests; migration conformance and native verification recorded in docs.
notes: Representative commits: 'docs: specify additive scoped events on the ordinary OpenCode stream', 'Consume negotiated additive scoped events on ordinary OpenCode uplink', 'docs: align gateway operation with ordinary scoped event streams', 'Document ordinary scoped uplink and preserved distributor contracts', 'docs: record additive event migration conformance and native verification', 'fix(gateway): expose scope capability to browser clients'. Design: design/event-multiplexer/additive-events.md.

title: Gateway crate: source ownership, native auth, and streaming transport
description: bus-proxy-gateway owns the sole origin uplink (GET /api/event with OpenCode-Event-Scope negotiation, readiness sequencing, capped reconnect backoff), native-compatible Basic/query/pairing-cookie auth with CORS, local SSE feeds with heartbeats, transparent HTTP forwarding with WebSocket upgrade tunnels, bounded connection admission, header-read expiry, and setup-only upstream deadlines that never cut off API execution or uploads. Inbound Host never selects the uplink; obvious listener self-targets rejected.
acceptance_criteria: Loopback suite passes: scope negotiation/rejection, spoofed-payload authority, failure/truncation/oversize/idle handling, reconnection and stale IDs, two-proxy raw JSON, auth/CORS/cookies, streaming uploads, cancellation, tunnels, budgets, redacted tracing.
notes: Representative commits: 'Implement gateway source ownership, native auth and streaming transport', 'Harden gateway source aliases, upgrade validation and bounded interest errors', 'Fix ordinary forwarding deadlines: bound connection setup, not execution or uploads', 'Bound admitted HTTP connections and upgrade lifetimes; expire idle request headers'. Docs: crates/gateway/README.md.

title: Protocol crate: bounded SSE decoding and native wire adapters
description: bus-proxy-protocol owns ordinary scoped events, the shared selection contract, control and SSE decoding, and raw event frames shared with subscribers. Bounded incremental decoding counts non-newline frame bytes including comments/field prefixes; decode preserves native permissiveness for ignored fields and duplicate keys; shared fixtures (event-scope-v1.json) match the native copy byte-for-byte.
acceptance_criteria: Wire-boundary tests pass; native fixture hash equality; oversized/truncated frames rejected without unbounded allocation.
notes: Representative commits: 'feat(protocol): implement bounded SSE and native wire adapters', 'test(protocol): cover wire boundaries and document decode semantics', 'fix(protocol): preserve native ignored-field and duplicate-key permissiveness'.

title: Router crate: indexed epoch-scoped routing with bounded subscriber queues
description: bus-proxy-router owns the session index, atomic interest replacement, bounded per-subscriber queues (frames and bytes), and epoch invalidation. Interest replacement is atomic at proxy admission; queued frames keep their old recipient decision. Source epoch retirement invalidates downstream queues and subscription IDs. Shared frame bytes avoid per-recipient copies; release benchmark measures in-process throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Router unit tests including panic cleanup and cancellation barriers pass; benchmark invocation documented; native subscription-ID schema conformance.
notes: Representative commits: 'feat: implement indexed epoch-scoped router with bounded subscriber queues', 'test: verify router panic cleanup and cancellation barriers', 'fix: conform subscription IDs to native schema and retain lifecycle spans'. Docs: crates/router/README.md, doc/event-multiplexer/verification.md.

title: Ship opencode-bus-proxy: standalone scoped-event gateway (v1)
description: The complete v1 effort: a standalone Rust gateway that moves OpenCode V2 event selection and fan-out out of the Session execution server. Ordinary scoped-event uplink from the bus-smart origin, an indexed epoch router with bounded queues, native-compatible auth and CORS, transparent HTTP forwarding with WebSocket tunnels, authenticated diagnostics, real-client compatibility verification, operations docs, systemd integration, and public release under MIT. Canonical architecture lives in bus-smart; this repo owns the optional gateway.
acceptance_criteria: Workspace green (fmt/clippy/tests); compatibility suite passes against real bus-smart and legacy clients; operations docs current; published at github.com/rektide/opencode-bus-proxy.
notes: Children cover each shipped workstream. Tip at publication: 2afd1ea7.

title: Report sd_notify readiness, status, stopping, and watchdog heartbeats
description: Type=notify units receive READY=1 (with the listening address as STATUS=) once the gateway accepts connections, and STOPPING=1 when shutdown begins. WATCHDOG_USEC (set by WatchdogSec=) schedules WATCHDOG=1 datagrams at half the configured timeout; the watchdog is process liveness only - source readiness stays with /_bus/health, and WatchdogSec= should outlast source reconnect backoff. NOTIFY_SOCKET may be abstract-namespace ('@' prefix), sent via libc sendto; without a manager, notify is a successful no-op.
acceptance_criteria: Datagram lifecycle READY=1 -> WATCHDOG=1 -> STOPPING=1 observed against a real receiver; abstract and filesystem sockets both deliver; no manager changes nothing.
notes: Shipped: commit 8fa7449e. Verified by unit tests (filesystem + abstract loopbacks) and a live SIGTERM lifecycle smoke. Docs: operations.md 'systemd service integration'.

title: Read the shared password from systemd credentials by name
description: --credential (env BUS_PROXY_CREDENTIAL) names a systemd credential: the daemon reads $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/<name>, provided by any of LoadCredential=, LoadCredentialEncrypted=, SetCredential=, or ImportCredential= (systemd >=247; >=250 for encrypted). Credential names are validated filename-safe (leading letter/digit, then [A-Za-z0-9._-]) before joining, so a misconfigured name cannot traverse; trailing CR/LF is trimmed like --password-file; --password-file and --credential together is rejected; missing/empty directory errors name the unit directives.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon authenticates with a LoadCredential= unit password; --credential with no $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY gives an actionable error; traversal names like ../escape rejected.
notes: Shipped: commits 1b25e755 (code+tests) and 4e9f867d (docs). Verified by daemon unit tests and binary smoke runs. Docs: operations.md 'Credentials and browser compatibility'.

title: Adopt the listening socket from systemd socket activation
description: When the service manager passes a listening socket (LISTEN_PID/LISTEN_FDS per sd_listen_fds(3)), the gateway adopts descriptor 3 instead of binding. The socket unit's ListenStream= owns the address: an explicit --listen/BUS_PROXY_LISTEN alongside activation is a configuration error. Non-internet handovers (e.g. ListenFIFO=) are rejected with an actionable error; the activation environment is consumed after adoption; a closed descriptor is a clean error, not an abort.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon serves from a .socket unit without --listen; explicit --listen + activation rejected; non-socket fd 3 rejected naming ListenStream=.
notes: Shipped: commit ac9fd399. Verified by daemon unit tests plus an end-to-end fd-passing exec smoke. Docs: doc/event-multiplexer/operations.md, 'systemd service integration'.
